english: Father, I am going to war. Do not weep for me. If I die, my name will be famous, and you will speak it. If I live, I will come back home. My horse will live with you. May you live many winters. -- My son, go! May the gods give you great fame and protect you.
uncertain: kóryom: ACC of goal 'to war'; lexicon 'war, troops'
ḱóymom: lexicon gives only adjective 'homely, belonging to the family'; read as noun 'home' (ACC of goal)
méne toy márkos tḱéyti: toy GEN or DAT enclitic; read DAT 'with you'; tḱéyti 'dwells' (present used for future)
méne súHnew: speaker changes here; the father answers

english: Fathers, five men are standing in our village. They ask us for water. Will they be our guests? Then the chief said: 'Our cattle are not many.' Then the chief said: 'Whoever kills a guest, the gods kill him. Sit at our fire, and let them eat and drink. Let them come as guests and go as friends.'
uncertain: ph₂téres nos: read as VOC 'Fathers' with nos going with wóyḱoy 'our village'; NOM 'our fathers, five men, stand' is possible but makes less sense
gʰósteyes: 'guests' or 'strangers, enemies'; the question plays on both
sékʷt: AOR.3SG of sekʷ- 'say' (vs. 'follow'); may be the same chief or a second one
gʷʰodʰéyonti: lexicon entry has no gloss; root gʷʰedʰ- 'request, pray, ask for'
misfit: sddʰí: 2SG imperative 'sit down' but the guests are referred to in 3PL (h₁déntu, ph₃éntu) and no singular addressee is present; expected 3PL/2PL

english: Your man killed my brother. Bring me ten bulls. That is the payment for my brother. If you bring them, I will be friendly to you. If you do not bring them, I will march against you. -- I hear you. I am bringing the bulls. May the pledge stay between us.
uncertain: moréyet: PST (imperfect) of 'kill', read as a completed killing
stigʰnéwoh₂: no gloss; root steygʰ- 'go, climb', read 'march'
m̥néh₁yoyh₁t: no gloss; root men- 'stay, remain' (lexicon id -2), read 'may it remain'
twé ḱl̥néwmi: speaker change, the other party answers

english: Go! Father Dyeus is the giver of good things; may he give you great fame. May they not be afraid. Do not flee from the fight. Grow strong! May Dawn shine for you. Remember your father.
uncertain: h₁uséwōm: GEN.PL 'of good things'
kh₃téws: GEN/ABL; read ABL 'from the fight'
lukyéh₁t: lexicon 'become bright'; read 'shine'
misfit: bʰebʰih₂ih₁ént: 3PL optative 'may they not fear' has no referent; everything around it addresses one person (2SG), so 2SG 'may you not fear' is expected

english: I slew the serpent. Who are you? My arm is swift and my heart is great. Come forth! If you overcome me, take my horses. If I overcome you, dogs and wolves will eat you. -- You speak many words. My arm will speak. Whoever dies, undying fame will remain for him.
uncertain: gʷʰénm̥: PST.1SG (imperfect) 'was slaying'; read as completed 'slew'
polh₁úh₂ wékʷōs bʰéh₂si: probably the other party replying
m̥néh₁yēti: no gloss; root 'stay, remain'

english: Hear me. Those who fell lie over there. Let us burn them with fire and lament them. Give me the pledge. -- I give it. Fire, listen to us.
uncertain: dédh₃dʰi / dédeh₃mi: reduplicated present 'give'
tā́m: ACC.SG.F 'it' referring to the pledge (bʰoydʰéh₂, feminine)
misfit: bʰoydʰéh₂s: GEN/ABL.SG, but as object of dédh₃dʰi 'give' it should be ACC bʰoydʰéh₂m; the next sentence picks it up with ACC tā́m

english: Hear me. Two swift horses carry me. The wheel of the sun is bright. I yoked my team at dawn. No one keeps up with me. Come to my field! Dawn, daughter of Sky, watch over us. Swift horses will not save you. My arm will seize you, and your chariot will break.
uncertain: kʷís me ne sékʷetor: ends in a period, so read as 'no one follows me' (ne + kʷis); a rhetorical 'who does not follow me?' is also possible; sékʷetor MID.PRS 'follows' or MID.SBJV of sekʷ- 'say'
kʷékʷlos: 'wheel' or 'chariot'; 'wheel' for the sun, 'chariot' at the end
Hrunépetor: MID.SBJV 'will be broken'

english: Brothers, the king is coming with ten swift horses. Where shall we stand? Then the chief said: 'Let us stand on that hill. The hill protects us, and horses do not climb it.' -- 'He who sits on it has won no fame.' -- 'Fear will seize them. Let us strike them at dawn. Let us go down to the field. Father Dyeus, give us great fame.'
uncertain: HHḱéwbʰis: unusual INS.PL of HeHḱus 'swift' (expected something like HeHḱúbʰis); the meaning is clear
h₁yós tósmi sédyeti só ḱléwos ne wént: read as an objection from someone else; gnomic aorist 'wins no fame'
trómos: no gloss; root trem- 'tremble', read 'fear'
speaker changes are not marked

english: You have come. Where is your brother? -- He lies over there; he fell. -- Did he stand his ground or flee? -- He stood. He did not flee. -- Undying fame will remain for him, and my heart weeps.
uncertain: bʰéwgt: 'flee' (bʰewg- 3) vs 'benefit' (bʰewg- 4); 'flee' fits

english: I have a daughter. Let your brother be my son-in-law. Give the bride-price. -- I give the bride-price, and I will send gifts and seven bulls. -- May she be dear to my brother. Dawn, lead her home. Sun, witness this pledge. May the two of them be dear to each other.
uncertain: séh₂ méne bʰréh₂trey: read as said by the second speaker (the groom's brother) about the groom; the speaker changes are not marked
wédʰe: 'lead, bring' or 'marry'
dedr̥ḱdʰí: 'see', read 'witness'
lewbʰóh₁: NOM.DU 'the two (are) dear' read; INS.SG 'in friendship/dearly' with 3PL 'they' would also work
misfit: h₁sih₁ént (low confidence): 3PL optative with what is most naturally a dual subject lewbʰóh₁; a dual verb is expected unless lewbʰóh₁ is INS.SG

english: My brothers, my brother sent word: 'Come! The king is attacking me.' Then the chief said: 'We have a village and bulls. Let us not go.' Then the chief said: 'Our brother's war is ours. If he dies, they will come for us. I will march. Who will follow me?' -- 'I will follow you.' -- 'Mother Earth, protect my brother. May he live and may they fall.'
uncertain: sélǵet: no gloss; root selǵ- 'let go, send'; PST read 'sent'
stunédti: 'push, hit'; read 'attacks'
h₂éǵt: AOR 'said'; a different chief from the first, or the same one
gʷm̥yṓnti nos: 'they will come (against) us'

english: Are you alive? -- I am alive. -- Is your fame great? -- My fame is not great. I have come back. -- My heart rejoiced. Sit at our fire and drink water.
uncertain: the speaker changes are guessed

english: Dog! You stole my cattle in the night. You are not a man. Come! Dogs will eat you. Run! -- I am a dog, and I protect the sheep. You are the wolf. You drove off my cattle last year. Now I will take them back.
uncertain: stéh₂yes: PST.2SG 'stole'
h₁époh₂: SBJV.1SG 'I will seize'; 'take back' is inferred

english: Your words are many. I have seen many winters and I know war. A young horse does not know the yoke. Seven young men came to that field, and now they lie there. I do not fear you. Go to your mother! Either farm (stay settled), or learn how to fight.
uncertain: tḱidʰí-wē kéh₃tum-kʷe h₁ukdʰí: -wē 'or' on the first verb and -kʷe on kéh₃tum; read 'either settle/farm, or learn fighting'; tḱidʰí 'settle, dwell, cultivate'
h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs: plural of 'young', used as a noun 'young men'

english: You have come back. Where did you go? -- I went by ship. -- What did you see? -- I saw seven villages. -- Are you bringing gifts? -- I am bringing gifts for you. -- Sit. My heart rejoiced.
uncertain: kúdʰe: 'where?' used with a motion verb, read 'where to'

english: Fathers, you know this pledge. The king of the hill made a pledge with us and broke it. What shall we do? -- The gods will strike them. Let us wait. -- The gods have seen the pledge, and a man's arm strikes. Let us be the arm of the gods. Fire, burn them! Let us march.
uncertain: widé: IMP.2SG 'see!' or PRF.2PL 'you know'; ph₂téres is plural, so PRF.2PL fits; if 'see!' was meant, the number is wrong
Hrunépt: PST of nasal present, read 'broke'
m̥néh₁yōmes: 'let us stay/remain', read 'wait'
h₂n̥rés-kʷe bʰeh₂ǵʰús stunédti: GEN 'a man's arm strikes'; read as 'human hands must act'

english: You march away, and I will stay. Wear this garment, which I made for you from my wool. I will watch you from the hill. May Fire lead you. May the sun warm you.
uncertain: dʰéh₁m̥: 'put, place, do'; read 'made'
gʷʰr̥yéh₁t: 'become warm' with DAT tébʰye, 'be warm for you'

english: The priest said to the king: 'Sacrifice to the god Werunos.'
uncertain: ǵʰéwtōr: no gloss; root ǵʰew- 'pour', 'pourer' meaning libation priest
tom: unaccented ACC 'that/the'
h₁yáǵeswo: no gloss; root h₁yaǵ- 'sacrifice, worship', MID.IMP.2SG
wérunom: not analyzed; read as the proper name Werunos (ACC)

english: Father and mother, hear me. I am going, and my brother will live with you. Protect my wife. If I fall, do not weep. Burn me. May you live.
uncertain: 2PL forms (ḱluté, ph₂sté, HrudHté, dʰégʷʰete, gʷíh₃woyh₁te) for two addressees where a dual might be expected; used consistently
wos: DAT.ENCL 'with you' (could also be GEN 'your')
dʰégʷʰete: PRS/IMP 2PL; read as imperative 'burn (cremate) me'

english: Brothers, winter is coming. Shall we go to war now? Then the chief said: 'If we go, we will strike them. If we sit still, the snow will kill us. They will freeze.' Then the chief said: 'Snow lies on our field. Who will feed our cattle? Let us stay and feed them. When the snow melts and the sun grows warm, then we will march. Our fame will be great.'
uncertain: tóy stéwdonti: 'they will become cold'; who 'they' are (the enemy or our men) is unclear
h₁yód: 'if' in the first chief's speech, 'when' in the last sentence
the two 'chief said' lines may be two different chiefs

english: Brother, you have come! You have been gone nine winters. We said: 'He has perished.' Our mother wept for you. Now I see you, and my heart rejoiced. -- I am well. I was living in a village over there.
uncertain: wr̥h₁mé. néḱt.: read 'we said: he is lost'
tḱḗm: PST.1SG of tḱey- 'dwell' (lengthened form)

english: Serpent, you devoured my cattle and you devoured my brother. Come out of your hill! I do not fear you. Father Dyeus, give me power. I will split you. Sun, watch the serpent. -- Who are you? Ten men came at me. I devoured them, and I will eat you too. Now undying fame will be mine.
uncertain: gʷr̥h₃és: PST.2SG 'were devouring', read as completed
séǵʰos: 'overpowering; control, power'
the serpent's reply begins at kʷís túH h₁ési
déh₃s: AOR.2SG without augment; read as an injunctive prayer 'give me' rather than past 'you gave'

english: The Sheep and the Horses
uncertain: title; h₁éḱwōskʷe is written with -kʷe attached and no hyphen

english: Brothers, a man stands over there and shouts: 'Let a man come out to fight!' Who of you will go? -- No one speaks. They tremble. Then a young man stood up: 'I will go; I am not afraid.' -- 'He has killed ten men.' -- 'I will march.' -- 'Go now, and win good fame. May Fire protect you.'
uncertain: kʷís ne bʰéh₂ti: 'no one speaks'; bʰéh₂ti 'speak' vs 'shine' (bʰeh₂- 2)
só déḱm̥t wiHróns moréyet: 'he (the challenger) killed ten men', said by someone else as a warning
h₂nḗr kéh₃tum mélh₃tu: probably the challenger's shouted words

english: On a hill, a sheep that had no wool saw horses: one pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a great load, and one carrying a man swiftly.
uncertain: gʷr̥Hḗi: LOC of gʷr̥Hís (no gloss; root 'praise; elevate'); read 'on a hill/height'
wlh₂néH: not analyzed; read 'wool'
(h₁é) est: not analyzed; 'was', with an optional augment
spéḱet: not analyzed; read 'saw' (past of spéḱ- 'look')
méǵHm: not analyzed; read 'great' (ACC)
ǵʰménm̥: not analyzed; read 'man' (ACC, cf. ǵʰmṓ 'human')
Hṓḱu: not analyzed; read 'swiftly'
h₁oinom: spelled differently from the lexicon (h₁óynos); 'one'
this text uses a different spelling system from the others

english: Chief, let the hill be yours and the water mine. The field lies between us. Let your bulls drink at my water, and let my sheep graze in your field. -- Your word is good. So be it. As long as the sun goes and the earth stands, may our pledge remain.
uncertain: sóh₂wl̥ h₁éyti dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe stestóh₂e: literally 'the sun goes and the earth stands'; read as an oath formula 'as long as'
h₁déntu: 'let them eat', read 'graze'

english: Wife, raise our son. Let our fire be bright. Do not weep. If I do not come back, your husband's brother will protect you. Earth, give good things to her.
uncertain: pótnih₂: VOC 'lady, wife'
h₂éle: 'nourish', read 'raise'
misfit: lewkṓs: masculine NOM.PL 'bright', but péh₂wr̥ is neuter singular and h₁éstu is 3SG; expected neuter NOM.SG lewkóm

english: Husband, march off, and come back. May Fire lead you, and may your arm grow strong. I will sit at our fire and look for you at dawn. Dawn, daughter of Sky, lead him home. Remember me.
uncertain: wíHre: VOC 'man, husband'
tóm ḱóymom: ACC 'him' + 'home' (adjective used as a noun)
